REGIS REPORT

29 December 2025

We have a slew of macroeconomic news today:

 

  • The BSP adjusted its forecasts for the balance of payments (BOP) position of the country in 2025 and 2026 and a few things caught our attention. Although the BSP reduced its 2026 current account deficit forecast from US$15.5bn to US$15.3bn, the deficit is now projected to represent 3% of GDP (from 2.9% previously), implying that the BSP is forecasting weaker GDP growth in 2026. Furthermore, it raised its 2026 BOP deficit forecast from US$3.4bn, to US$5.9bn, likely signaling a weaker peso.  

 

  • Government infrastructure spending fell 33% YoY and 11% MoM in October and the government has indicated that it will be weak for the rest of 4Q25 as well, signaling that GDP growth for the period will likely be muted.  

 

  • The November trade deficit narrowed 29% YoY to US$3.5bn, reflecting the decline in imports and the robust growth of exports. Imports fell 2% YoY while exports climbed 21% YoY, thanks to a 51% surge in electronics exports. The 11M25 trade deficit fell 14% YoY to US$45.2bn

 

  • The bicameral conference committee has signed the report on the P6.79tn (+7% YoY) General Appropriations Bill (GAB) for 2026. President Marcos will review the document and is slated to sign it into law on January 5.

 

+++

 

Amidst the backdrop of the flood control corruption scandal, the November survey of the Social Weather Station showed that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s net trust rating deteriorated to -3% from +7% in August. In contrast, Vice President Sara Duterte's net trust rating improved to +31% in November from +25% in August.

 

Speaking of the flood control scandal, Rossana Fajardo resigned as a member of the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI), the agency tasked to investigate irregularities in flood control projects. She is the second ICI commissioner to resign in the past month, leaving ICI Chairman Andres Reyes Jr. as the sole commissioner.

 

+++

 

Megaworld (MEG PM) disposed of its 34% stake in Suntrust Resort Holdings (SUN PM) for P1.5bn. Suntrust is the partner of Megaworld’s parent, Alliance Global (AGI PM), in developing an integrated resort complex in PAGCOR Entertainment City.

 

Blackrock subsidiary Global Infrastructure Partners will acquire a 40% stake in Aboitiz InfraCapital (AIC), a wholly owned subsidiary of Aboitiz Equity Ventures (AEV PM), for P13.7bn. AIC’s businesses include: regional airports, industrial parks, cellular towers, data centers, as well as water-related services.

MACRO
BSP adjusts BOP forecasts for 2025 and 2026
  • The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) in its quarterly review, slightly adjusted its forecasts for the balance of payments (BOP) position of the country in 2025-2026, still projecting deficits in both the BOP position and current account (CA)
    • The assumed deficit is hinged on the sustained trade-in-goods gap and weaker services revenues alongside moderating FDI
  • For 2025, BSP projections (as % of GDP) for the overall BOP position and the CA deficit was slightly revised to -1.4% and -3.3% from -1.3% and -3.2%, respectively
    • The slight revisions were mainly driven by the faster growth expectations in exports at 9% vs 1%, previously—which was offset by the faster growth in imports at 3% vs 1%
  • 2026 saw a more significant revision with a much wider expected deficit in the BOP position at -1.2% vs -0.6% previously, while the CA deficit is forecasted to be slightly wider at -3.0% from -2.9%
    • With minimal revisions in the CA assumptions for 2026, the wider BOP deficit is driven by the lower financial account inflows expected at -US$11.7bn vs -US$14.4bn previously
      • The lower inflows reflect more cautious investor sentiment expected given "heightened global financial volatility"
  • The GIR for 2025 is expected to be higher at US$109bn vs US$105bn previously
    • A further increase is projected for next year to US$110bn vs US$106bn initially
    • The increase in GIR was likely prompted by the surge in gold prices as the BSP's gold holdings are up ~63% YoY as of Nov

 

 

MACRO
Trade deficit narrows to $3.5bn in Nov
  • The Nov trade deficit narrowed to US$3.5bn, contracting 29% YoY, reflecting the decline in imports and the robust growth of exports
    • This brings the 11M25 trade deficit to US$45.2bn, 14% narrower YoY
  • Imports for the month fell by 2% YoY to US$10.4bn, a slower decline vs the 7% decrease in Oct
    • The decline was primarily driven by the decrease in consumer goods (-6%) and fuel imports (-19%)
  • Exports climbed by 21% YoY to US$6.9bn, the eleventh consecutive month of YoY growth and accelerating from the 19% increase in Oct
    • Electronics exports surged by 51% YoY to $4.2bn
      • These made up the bulk of exports at 61% of the total
    • Meanwhile, non-electronics exports were down 7% to US$2.7bn

 

 

 

 

 

 

MACRO
Government infrastructure spending extends decline in October
  • Overall infrastructure spending (i.e. disbursements from national government, LGUs, and GOCCs) fell 11.5% YoY to P1.129tn in 10M25
    • Derived infra spend for October alone stood at P88.7bn, down 33% YoY and 11% MoM
    • Cited delays in settlement of progress billings for public work’s projects amid the flood control corruption scandal
  • According to the DBM, subdued infrastructure spending should persist as a drag on total disbursements in 4Q25
  • Recall that the government has targeted to spend P1.5tn (+2% YoY, 5.3% of GDP) in 2025 and P1.56tn in 2026 (+3% YoY, 5.1% of GDP)
    • However, the bicam-approved General Appropriations Bill cut the Department of Public Works’ budget by P350bn, implying 2026 infrastructure spending could fall to P1.2tn (-20% YoY) from the proposed P1.56tn

 

 

MACRO
2026 budget bicam report finalized; budget signing by President eyed by Jan 5
  • The bicameral conference committee has signed the report on the P6.79tn (+7% YoY) General Appropriations Bill (GAB) for 2026, in-line with expectations to ratify the report by today (Dec 29, Monday)
  • President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was initially expected to sign the budget on the same day of ratification but disagreements on the Dept. of Public Works and Highways' allocated budget have prompted the President to need "at least one week review to carefully study and review the provisions"
  • The new target date to sign the 2026 GAA is now Jan 5, implying the need for a reenacted budget in the first few days of Jan
    • Senate finance committee head Sherwin Gatchalian stated that the short reenactment will have minimal impact on the country's economy
POLITICS
Marcos' net trust rating turns negative to -3% in Nov
  • In the November Social Weather Stations Survey, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s net trust rating deteriorated back into negative territory—falling to -3% from +7% back in Aug
    • Net figures are computed by % "much trust" rating minus % "little trust" rating
    • The movement to -3% is the same level as his net trust rating in Mar 2025 following the arrest of Former President Rodrigo Duterte
    • The president’s net trust rating has been declining since Jun, following Marcos’ disclosure of the flood-control scandal during his end-Jul SONA
  • Vice President Sara Duterte's net trust rating has improved 7ppt to 31% in Nov from 25% in Aug
    • The 38% net trust rating of the VP is much lower than her 73% net trust rating at the start of her term
      • But reflects an improvement for her 23% rating when she was impeached by the Lower House in Feb 2025

MACRO
Rossana Fajardo resigns as ICI commissioner
  • Rossana Fajardo has resigned as a member of the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI), the agency tasked to investigate irregularities in flood control projects
    • This follows fellow ICI commissioner Rogelio Singson's recent resignation earlier this month
  • Fajardo has stated that she has completed the work she set out to accomplish, ensuring that "the foundational goals of the Commission have been met"
    • She highlighted contributions on recommendations of improving gov't procurement and budgeting processes for infra projects
  • She also added that investigative and prosecutorial responsibilities should now be handled by agencies with permanent mandates—the Dept. of Justice (DOJ) and the Office of the Ombudsman
  • Fajardo is the country managing partner at SGV & Co. and has been with the firm for over two decades
PROPERTY
Megaworld disposes of stake in Suntrust Resort
  • Megaworld sold its entire 34% stake in Suntrust Resort Holdings (SUN PM)
  • It sold 2.45bn SUN shares at P0.60/sh-P0.61/sh
  • Total value of c. P1.5bn
  • Suntrust Resort Holdings is the partner of Alliance Global in developing an integrated resort project in PAGCOR Entertainment City
    • In 3Q25, SUN recorded a P27bn loss in relation to the restructuring of its ownership in the said integrated resort project
  • MEG currently offers 4.4% dividend yield and is trading at 68% discount to NAV, 0.2X FY26E P/B, and 3.2X FY26E P/E   
CONGLOS
Blackrock’s GIP acquires 40% stake in subsidiary of Aboitiz Equity Ventures
  • Blackrock subsidiary Global Infrastructure Partners will acquire a 40% stake in Aboitiz InfraCapital (AIC), a wholly owned subsidiary or Aboitiz Equity Ventures (AEV PM)
    • GIP will acquire a total of 1,146,668,000 common shares and 1,408,000,000 redeemable preferred shares in AIC
  • Total price of P13.7bn
    • P4.65bn will be paid to AIC directly
    • P9.06bn will be paid to AEV
  • AIC’s main businesses are:
    • Administrative franchises to provide water and wastewater-related services to customers in Batangas, Cebu and Davao, among others,
    • Digital infrastructure, which includes common towers and data centers,
    • Regional airports
    • Economic estate projects
CONGLOS
LT Group subsidiary to list by way of introduction
  • LT Group disclosed that its 56.5% owned subsidiary, PNB Holdings Corporation (PHC), will list by way of introduction
    • PHC is 49% owned by Philippine National Bank (PNB PM)
  • The primary assets of PHC are:
    • PNB Financial Center along Diosdado Macapagal Boulevard in Pasay City – land area of about 10 hectares
    • PNB Center along Ayala Avenue in Makati City – land area of about 2,000sqm
    • A parcel of land at the intersection of Paseo de Roxas and Gil Puyat Avenue in Makati City – about 8,000sqm
MARKET
Foreign ownership of Philippine market rises in November
  • We estimate that foreign ownership of the overall market rose 33 bps MoM to 18.9% (in November) while foreign ownership of the PSE Index fell 14bps MoM to 23.6%
    • The increase in foreign ownership of the overall market was partly due the 21% MoM share price decline of Villar Land/Golden MV Holdings (HVN PM), which has zero foreign ownership (and a market cap of P1.17trn as of end-November 2025)
  • Foreign activity reversed from net selling of US$100mn in October to net foreign buying of US$78mn, largely thanks to the IPO of Maynilad Water Services (MYNLD PM) 
  • Among the PSEi constituents, 9 saw increases in foreign ownership while 20 experienced declines
  • The notable movements among PSEi constituents were:
    • JFC – Foreign ownership fell 67bps MoM to 20.3%, as net foreign selling hit US$21.2mn, the seventh highest for the month.   
    • ALI – foreign ownership declined 58bps MoM to 23.7%, as net foreign selling reached US$29.7mn, the second highest for the month.   
    • MBT – foreign ownership decreased 56bps MoM to 20.0%, as net foreign selling hit US$22.6mn, the fifth highest for the month. 
    • AREIT – foreign ownership climbed 32bps MoM to 4.5%, as it saw net foreign buying of US$7.5mn, the fifth highest for the month.
    • PLUS – foreign ownership increased 30bps MoM to 23.3%, as it experienced the highest net foreign buying for the month (US$151.4mn).
